detail: Stahl und Eisen, July 1, 1895, pp. 614–615 and Plate VIII. Gives a 15 m width, 32 m overall length and 30 m from base to tower cross. Visible in the plate are five repeating nave bays, entrance steps, the tall square bell chamber and domed spire, and short projecting transept.

The Bulgarian Orthodox Patriarchate describes architect Hovsep Aznavur’s three-aisled basilica with barrel vault and one five-sided apse, assembled from parts made by Waagner. The church was consecrated in 1898.

The Istanbul municipal conservation team describes dismantling and renewing zinc roof coating, recasting lost decorative iron panels, and conserving the façade framing, leaded glazing and external cast pieces.
The 2019 steel award records the surviving ornamental prefabricated iron church, cast, wrought and rolled components and the restoration funded by Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality.
This architectural study records a greenish grey exterior following the 2018 restoration.
